name: Two-Coefficient-Row Feasibility Criterion
statement: For a blocked pair of positive normalized rows $p,q$ at concept $c$, let $I=I_c(p)$ and $J=I_c(q)$. A positive witness exists exactly when $\max_{i\in I}a_{p,i}/a_{q,i}>\min_{j\in J}a_{p,j}/a_{q,j}$, equivalently when $a_{p,i}a_{q,j}>a_{q,i}a_{p,j}$ for some $i\in I,j\in J$. Rational feasible rows admit an explicit rational witness.
proof: If the maximum ratio does not exceed the minimum, chaining the two strict row inequalities gives a contradiction. Conversely, choose a strict determinant pair, put positive weight one on its first coordinate, choose the second weight strictly between the two ratios, and give all remaining coordinates sufficiently small positive rational weights.
